summary: Mono National Forest lookout built 1940 on Mogul Peak near Markleeville; the register says only the foundation remains and gives no removal date.

facts.design: Described by the register as a unique design; a 1940 newspaper says the building was insulated with copper wire against lightning
facts.status_note: Removal date unknown; the register says only the foundation remains
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mono National Forest, now Toiyabe National Forest)

access.note: On Toiyabe National Forest land per the register; no access restriction described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: A trail guide lists a 15.5-mile out-and-back from the Barney Riley Trail trailhead that reaches Mogul Peak

notes_for_editor: The record's kind 'ground' (from FFLA) is not confirmed by any source read; the 1940 newspapers say only 'lookout building' and do not mention a tower or a ground cabin. The 'only the foundation remains' line is undated and no later source was found. The 1940 paper places the lookout about four miles east of Markleeville; the register places it atop Mogul Peak, and the trail guide reaches Mogul Peak, so the two are treated as the same site. The trail guide shows a route, not whether the foundation is visible from it. No photo of the site today was found.
